doc.title: JJ Johnson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Hearing the Nat King Cole Trio at the Three Sixes
summary: The band heard the Cole trio before they were famous and were astonished by the arrangements and Nat's piano.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Working with Sinatra: bands, Vegas and the Sands

blocks.x: How about that. I’ll tell you, I would like to recall this incident that happened while we were at Billy Berg's Swing Club. We heard about a place where a trio was playing that was a mind-blowing experience, to go hear this trio.
I know who you're talking about, yeah.

Yeah. We went to a club called the Three Sixes, 666, and the trio was the Nat "King" Cole Trio. And the word was true. It blew our minds. The musicality and the beauty of this trio. The complex arrangements they played. Nat and that wonderful voice and what not. He was quite a pianist.

His main bag was as a jazz pianist. They did a lot of instrumentals and very few vocals, as a matter of fact. But he did sing once in a while at the Three Sixes. This is before he had made his mark. This is before he hit the big time. He was just another trio in Los Angeles playing at a venue in Los Angeles, but something special, something very special. It could have been projected or predicted that this is going to go someplace. As we all know, history will show that it did indeed go someplace.
It must have been very attractive when with Jazz at the Philharmonic he was the piano player behind you guys on a lot of those things.
Oh, man, he was some piano player. He was some accompanist, rather.
I remember those Jazz at the Philharmonic recordings with you, and Nat's playing piano on them, man.
